answer: Each claim must survive an echo: a stranger re-runs the work and the echo must match, and the claimant pays the echo fee up front. Every identity holds a lagoon lease, a deposit locked in a shared still-water pool that releases only when echoes come back clean; the lease is per identity and cannot be split. Verified echoes are carved into basalt, and payout grows with basalt depth, so a fresh clone starts at zero and earns the lowest rate. Echoes from one funding trail are charged together, so n clones pay n squared in echo fees while one lagoon's payout is fixed and split n ways.
